definition.simple: A process to separate a mixture of two liquids by boiling them. The liquid that boils first turns into gas, is captured, and cooled back into a liquid.
definition.academic: The action of purifying a liquid by a process of heating and cooling, specifically used to separate miscible liquids that boil without decomposition and have sufficient difference in their boiling points.

examples: Separating a mixture of acetone (low boiling point) and water (high boiling point).

common_misconceptions: Distillation can separate any two liquids. (False: It only works well if their boiling points differ by more than 25 Kelvin. Otherwise, Fractional Distillation is used).
ai_context.tutor_hint: Distillation relies on the fact that one liquid is 'eager' to boil before the other one!
